subcommittees.name: Economic Development, Public Buildings, and Emergency Management Subcommittee

dimensions.assessment: States, local governments, and individuals demonstrating financial need who receive residential resilience grants.
dimensions.evidence: a pilot program for states and local governments to provide grants to individuals for residential resilience retrofits

dimensions.assessment: Provides eligible individuals with targeted financial assistance for home resilience retrofits and gives local governments flexibility in building code editions.
dimensions.evidence: projects that increase a home’s resilience to natural hazards

dimensions.assessment: Reallocates up to 10% of annual BRIC program assistance for the pilot program without authorizing new appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator may use not more than 10 percent of the assistance made available to applicants on an annual basis

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act regarding building code requirements and establishes a temporary pilot program.
dimensions.evidence: Section 203 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5133) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent changes for building code eligibility under FEMA programs, while the residential retrofit pilot program terminates on September 30, 2030.
dimensions.evidence: the program shall terminate on September 30, 2030

missing_information: Total dollar amounts of annual funding available under the BRIC program.
Exact number of individuals or local jurisdictions expected to participate.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill modifies existing FEMA hazard mitigation programs to allow local governments to use funds for the latest two editions of building codes instead of only the latest edition, and establishes a temporary residential resilience retrofit pilot program using up to 10% of annual BRIC program funds until September 30, 2030.
